chapter: Closing and the Al Wynn band
title: Two lost years and joining Al Wynn's band
summary: He sums up losing his horn for two years after the lip operation, and says Al Wynn and Frankie coaxed him back into a small group about three years ago.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: I have the record well I think that covers pretty much all of your life on that especially all that New Orleans man that you worked with I'm certainly glad to hear all that history unless you have something else to add no that's about all

you see that's about all you see the only thing I lost track was those two years I lost my horn when I had the operation on my lip well you're lucky to come through that right and get your lip back that's right you see and then you see usually when I feel like people lost track of me as playing as a jazz trumpet and then I come back by me being able to read and I knew the trumpet yeah they put you on that first part like you say
where they that's it to read all that yes how long have you been with Al Wynn now? this band

well we've been out this band about three years now about three years well you see I had to put down the horn you had to put it down for a while oh I put it down again I mean I stopped again put the horn down again and it was through Al Al told Frankie to try and get me to go and pick up my horn and come back and start the playing again and Frankie come and I said oh man I said I don't know I'm messing with horn no more I've been around Chicago for years and never heard of you so I didn't know whether you were still working or not so he said well I'm going to have a small group well I said alright if you're going to have a small group alright get me to play because I know if it's going to be a big group I still wouldn't get a chance to play my horn the way I was going to play. the same thing like when I was going to Earl High I played Earl High it's the same identical thing but Earl the first thing you do is put it on the first trumpet
